newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Property gloom sees Singapore shares close down.
newsitem.headline: Property gloom sees Singapore shares close down.

text.p: Singapore shares closed weaker on Wednesday with waning sentiment in the property sector dampening demand marketwide, dealers said.
"The property market has a powerful voice in Singapore and it dampened sentiment across the market today," one dealer said.
The Stock Exchange of Singapore property index sank 12.35 or 1.78 percent to end at 682.15, sparking a fall on the Straits Times Industrials Index of 10.69 points to 1,966.41.
Dealers said the falls were caused by a letter from the Real Estate Developers Association of Singapore to the Minister of National Development predicting a collapse in the market.
"It has not been a good day and there is no sign that tomorrow will be any better," another dealer said of a trading day that saw losers swamp gainers 219 to 119.
Central Properties reflected the gloom, shedding Singapore $1.50 to S$17.50, and Bukit Sembawang Estates dropped a dollar to S$24.00.
Singapore Land managed a 10-cent gain to S$7.40 despite the gloom of its fellow property firms.
Small cap and electronics stocks were most active.
IPC Corp saw 14.9 million shares traded, almost 10 percent of the market total of 161 million, to end the day up nine cents at S$0.54.
